chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Amr ibn Uthman and Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Uthafir, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the night prayer and the Witr prayer after the rising of Fajr (dawn). He said: 'Pray it after Fajr, so that it is in a time when you would pray the morning prayer (al-Ghadat) at its end, and do not make it a habit every night.' And he said: 'Also perform Witr after you have finished from it.'

key_terms.الْغَدَاةَ: The morning prayer (specifically referring to Salat al-Fajr or the morning time)

ai.seo_question: How should the night prayer and Witr be performed after dawn rises according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the flexibility of Salat al-Layl by permitting its performance after Fajr sunrise, specifically aligning it with the preferred time of delaying the Fajr prayer (Akhir al-Waqt), while cautioning against making this delay a permanent habit to avoid resembling the practices of other sects. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on balancing spiritual devotion with practical ease, distinguishing it from the Hanafi tradition of fixed Witr timing and reinforcing the concept of 'Tasbih al-Fadl' as a distinct, recommended act performed after the main night prayers.
